The proposal uses the first-person singular 'I' in nearly every section (Abstract, Objective 4.x, Schedule, AI Transparency), typically in constructions like 'I develop…', 'I implement…', 'I evaluate…', 'I reach this objective when…', 'I deliver…'. The thesis-approach statements should use 'we' (e.g., 'In this thesis, we develop…'), and system-behaviour descriptions should name the platform, the chair, or another concrete actor as the subject. The AI Transparency section may retain 'I' for personal disclosure, but the main body (Abstract through Schedule) should not.

locations.quote: In this thesis, **I develop** a self-service platform on which every grant carries an expiry date from the moment somebody requests it.
**I evaluate** the platform at the chair on correctness, administrative effort, and extensibility.
In this thesis, **I develop** a self-service platform on which requesters ask for time-limited access, maintainers decide, and access ends on its own
**I pursue** four objectives:
**I model** the resources as a tree whose folders pass maintainership, audit policy, and grants down to leaves bound to target systems
**I implement** the keycloak-group, slack-channel, github-team, and webhook connectors, whose credentials administrators configure at runtime
**I reach** this objective when the webhook connector, written after **I freeze** the framework, needs one new class and one registry entry.
**I evaluate** correctness with an automated scenario that provisions SSH, Slack, and GitHub access from one approval.
Keycloak gates its workflow API on a realm-wide administrative role that maintainers must not hold, so **I split** each decision into a review step
**I reach** this objective when the platform answers, for any grant, who requested it and why, who reviewed and granted it, when it ended, and who confirmed it since.
**I divide** the work into six iterations of four weeks, each ending with a vertically integrated increment
Iteration 1, 1–28 October (Objective 1): **I deliver** the Keycloak realm with OpenID Connect login, SSH key self-service, and the resource tree with inherited maintainers.
